title: Command palette: find any feature, PRD or goal
subtitle: Mock-ups for issue 1794: ⌘K finds any item and runs an action. Three decisions, three proposals each. Invented example data. Open any frame with ?theme=dark for dark.

decisions.name: How the palette opens and looks
decisions.question: When a person presses ⌘K (Ctrl+K), what opens, and what does each result row show?
decisions.common: ⌘K or Ctrl+K opens it on every Simple and Detailed page; Esc closes it. Results come in groups (Features, PRDs, Goals, Key results, Milestones, Go to, Do); every feature shows its code with its name; Enter on a feature opens the one feature panel over the page you are on. Same story in each: find F-79 Weekly alert digest from Home.

proposals.name: Centered sheet
proposals.what: A sheet opens in the middle of the screen over a dimmed page, the box at the top. One line per result: an icon for its kind, the code and name, then its kind and where it lives on the right. A key strip at the foot says ↑↓ move, ↵ open, Tab more. On a phone it fills the screen.
proposals.why: It is the shape people know from other tools, it fits the most per row (code, name, kind and place on one line), and nothing on the page moves. Long names stay on one line, so many results still fit at 1512.
proposals.plus: Kind and place on every row; works the same on every page; full screen on a phone.
proposals.cost: 3 steps (⌘K, type, Enter) against 4 steps and a scroll today.

frames.caption: Home today, with no palette open.
⌘K: the sheet opens in the middle with recent items, actions and pages.
Typing “weekly alert”: F-79 Weekly alert digest is first, with its kind and track.
Enter: the feature panel of F-79 opens over Home. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case at 1512: 60 more features with long names; 5 per group, then “more”.
Phone: the sheet fills the screen; rows drop the place to keep the name.

proposals.name: Drop-down from the top
proposals.what: The box drops down from the top of the page, not the middle, with a strong outline and no dark cover: the page stays readable under it. Kind is the group title only; each row shows the code, the name and where it lives.
proposals.plus: The page stays visible; it reads like a search field people already use.
proposals.cost: 3 steps (⌘K, type, Enter), same as a; less room per row for the kind.

frames.caption: Home before ⌘K, the same start as a.
⌘K: the box drops from the top; the page stays bright under it.
Typing “weekly alert”: one row for F-79, with its track on the right.
Enter: the F-79 panel opens over Home. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case at 1512 on Roadmap: long names cut to one line; the page shows through.
Phone: the box drops from the top edge; the rest of the page is still under it.

proposals.name: Side sheet
proposals.what: A tall sheet slides in from the right, like the feature panel. Each result takes two lines: the code and the full name (up to two lines), then its kind and where it lives. It shows 8 per group, not 5. On a phone it is a bottom sheet.
proposals.plus: Full long names; more results per group; feels like the panel it opens.
proposals.cost: 3 steps (⌘K, type, Enter); twice the height per row, so fewer kinds fit without scrolling.

frames.caption: Home before ⌘K, the same start as a.
⌘K: a sheet slides in from the right with recent items, actions and pages.
Typing “weekly alert”: F-79 with its kind and track on a second line.
Enter: the sheet gives way to the F-79 panel on the same side. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case at 1512: long names wrap to two lines; 8 shown, then “more”.
Phone: a bottom sheet with a handle, the page dimmed above it.

decisions.name: What it finds and does
decisions.question: What does the palette find, what happens on Enter, and what does it show when the box is empty or nothing matches?
decisions.common: It finds features by code or name, PRDs, goals, key results and milestones, and every page. Shown in the centered sheet (CP1 a). Actions follow the person's role through can(): a commenter's new item is a proposal, a viewer gets none.

proposals.name: Find and open here
proposals.what: Only finding. Enter on a feature opens its panel over the page you are on; a PRD, goal or milestone takes you to its page. The empty box shows recent items and pages. With no match it says so and how to search (a code or a word).
proposals.plus: Simplest to learn; nothing can change by accident.
proposals.cost: 3 steps (⌘K, “f-79”, Enter); adding an item still takes 4 steps on Roadmap.

frames.caption: ⌘K on Home: recent items and pages, nothing else.
Typing “f-79”: the code finds F-79 Weekly alert digest.
Enter: the F-79 panel opens over Home; you never left the page. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case, a commenter at 1512 types “quiet hours”: no match, and no way on from here.
Phone, opened from the header: recent items and pages.

proposals.name: Find and do
proposals.what: Finding plus actions in the same list: New item, New PRD, Ask Oracle, go to a page. Typing “new …” turns the words into a new item's title. Tab on a feature shows its own actions (open its panel, show it on the Roadmap, ask Oracle about it). With no match, Enter adds the words as an item, or Ask Oracle. A commenter sees “Propose a new item”; a viewer sees no add.
proposals.why: It is what the issue asks for (actions in the same box), it saves the most steps for the everyday add, and it keeps the role rule: owners and approvers add at once, commenters propose.
proposals.plus: One box for going and doing; no dead end on no match.
proposals.cost: Add an item: 3 steps (⌘K, “new …”, Enter) against 4 today; open a feature: 3 steps.

frames.caption: ⌘K on Home: recent items, then Do (New item, New PRD, Ask Oracle), then pages.
Typing “new Quiet hours for alerts”: New item with that title is first.
Enter: Roadmap opens with “Quiet hours for alerts” in Add an item, ready to place. Cost note at the foot.
Tab on F-79: its own actions, open its panel here, show it on Roadmap, ask Oracle.
Hard case, a commenter at 1512: the same words read “Propose a new item”; an approver decides.
Phone: the same list; Tab is not needed, a tap opens.

proposals.name: Go to its page
proposals.what: Finding takes you to where the item lives: Enter on a feature moves you to Roadmap (Plan in Detailed) and opens its panel there; the empty box lists pages only. With no match, Enter asks Oracle with your words.
proposals.plus: You always see the item in its place, next to its neighbours.
proposals.cost: 3 steps, but you leave the page you were on; going back is one more step.

frames.caption: ⌘K on Home: pages only, no recent items or actions.
Typing “weekly alert”: F-79 Weekly alert digest.
Enter: you are on Roadmap with the F-79 panel open. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case, a commenter at 1512 types “quiet hours”: no match, Enter asks Oracle.
Phone: the page list from the header button.

decisions.name: Reaching it without a keyboard
decisions.question: How does a person on a phone or with a mouse only open the palette?
decisions.common: The entry opens the same palette as ⌘K (CP1 a, CP2 b). It shows on Simple and Detailed and on the phone. Story: open it with a tap, find the goal Activation, go to Goal map.

proposals.name: Find in the rail
proposals.what: A Find row sits at the top of the Simple rail, above Home, with its ⌘K hint; Detailed's narrow rail gets a Find tile in the same place. On a phone a search button sits in the top bar beside Ask.
proposals.why: It lives where people already look for places, takes no room on the page, and teaches the ⌘K key by showing it.
proposals.plus: No room taken from pages; shows the shortcut.
proposals.cost: 1 tap or click to open, then the same steps as ⌘K.

frames.caption: Simple Home: Find with ⌘K at the top of the rail.
A click on Find opens the palette.
Typing “activation”: the goal Activation is first.
Enter: Goal map. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case, Detailed at 1512: a Find tile under the Simple and Detailed switch in the narrow rail.
Phone on Roadmap: a search button in the top bar, beside Ask.
Phone: a tap on it opens the palette full screen.

proposals.name: Field above every page
proposals.what: A slim strip above every page carries a search field (“Find a feature, PRD or goal ⌘K”), in Simple, Detailed and on the phone under the top bar.
proposals.plus: Impossible to miss; looks like search everywhere else.
proposals.cost: 1 click; but a 48px strip on every page, and on a phone it pushes the page down.

frames.caption: Simple Home: a search field in a strip above the page.
A click on the field opens the palette.
Typing “activation”.
Enter: Goal map, the strip still on top. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case, Detailed at 1512: the strip sits above Home's own header.
Phone on Roadmap: the strip under the top bar pushes the page down.
Phone: a tap on the field opens the palette.

proposals.name: Round Find button
proposals.what: A round Find button floats at the bottom right of every page; on a phone it sits above the tab bar.
proposals.plus: Always one tap away, at thumb reach on a phone.
proposals.cost: 1 tap; but it covers page corners (buttons, the panel's foot) on every page.

frames.caption: Simple Home: a round Find button at the bottom right.
A click on it opens the palette.
Typing “activation”.
Enter: Goal map; the button stays. Cost note at the foot.
Hard case, Detailed at 1512: the button sits over Home's rows.
Phone on Roadmap: the button above the tab bar covers the list.
Phone: a tap opens the palette full screen.
